scope_note: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Markley Group's Lowell data center at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County. The selected IM3 footprint is one building inside a three-building assessor parcel, so every added value remains at campus or company/county scope and is unallocated to the selected building. State and City records add Phase I forecasts, cumulative investment, operating-headcount, TIF-savings and incentive evidence; the assessor adds annual real-property values; MassDEP adds a permit-listed generator count; and a recipient page verifies one community contribution. Forecasts, cumulative values, parcel stocks, permit-authorized equipment, white-space area and recipient funding remain distinct and non-additive. Searches of planning and permit files, incentive and compliance reports, assessor and fiscal records, utility and environmental materials, operator disclosures, contractor and supplier pages, workforce and procurement records, community recipients, archives and repository county panels found no audited annual construction outlay, construction workforce or payroll, vendor payments or local-purchase share, facility payroll, metered annual electricity, project-attributable utility upgrade cost, annual water series matching the evidence vocabulary, wastewater, actual emissions, reconciled tax receipts, marginal public-service cost, fiscal net or causal county outcome. No model is added because the missing allocation and expenditure anchors cannot be bounded defensibly and Markley is not a clean first data-center entry in Middlesex County.

project_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — selected building kept separate from the campus
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: IM3 inventory geometry and provenance; Markley current and archived operator pages; Lowell assessor parcel P90290/MBLU 184/4765/2; 2015, 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024 City planning and bond records; deed/sale fields; and web archives. Exact identifiers included 2 Prince Avenue, 1 Markley Way, parcel 184/4765/2, assessor pid 47203 and IM3 source record 00214321737. The evidence supports a June 2015 purchase, Phase One open with customer occupancy by November 23, 2015, a three-building 14.4-acre assessor parcel, a later 65,000-square-foot expansion approval and continuing equipment changes. It does not map the selected 123,665-square-foot inventory footprint to an assessor building number or allocate campus investment, jobs, capacity, incentives or current white space to that polygon.
project_updates.project_description: Markley Group's Lowell data center operates at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County, Massachusetts, on the former Prince Pasta factory site. The selected IM3 footprint represents one building within a three-building assessor parcel, so campus-wide investment, employment, value, capacity, and incentive facts remain unallocated to that building. Markley reported Phase One open with customers occupying space by November 23, 2015 and now describes the Lowell facility as 352,000 square feet of secured white space. City planning records separately document a 2018 approval for a 65,000-square-foot expansion and later cooling, water-tank, generator, and utility modifications.

project_updates.title: Investment, incentive and fiscal audit — forecasts separated from cumulative observations
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: the 2015 EACC approval release; Lowell FY2020-FY2026 adopted budgets and TIF appendices; the 2023 preliminary official statement; EDIP awardee, annual-report, compliance and decertification pages; City Council packets; assessor history; and searches for the 2015 TIF agreement, personal-property exemption schedules, tax bills and collections. The fragment adds the $72.8 million Phase I plan, later $104,121,860 cumulative-investment observation, $77,182,505 combined local incentive forecast, $187,500 approved state credit, and $1,624,655.79 cumulative real-estate TIF savings. The baseline approximately $200 million campus and $12 million incremental-tax forecasts remain intact. The sources do not reconcile the $150 million and approximately $200 million proposal vintages, prove credit use, publish a personal-property exemption ledger, identify annual realized abatements, show property-tax bills or cash receipts, allocate City revenue among jurisdictions, quantify public-service cost, or support a net fiscal result.

project_updates.title: Assessor and parcel audit — four annual real-property stocks added
project_updates.notes: The official Vision Government Solutions Lowell portal was searched by Markley, Prince Avenue, Markley Way, parcel ID P90290, MBLU 184/4765/2 and property-record pid 47203. The card identifies Markley Group LLC, three buildings, 14.4 acres, a $3.85 million June 15, 2015 sale, and 2023-2026 total parcel values. The four total values are retained as one whole-parcel annual series. The sale price is not forced into an investment metric, individual building replacement-cost fields are not summed as economic activity, the 2026 value jump is not labeled new investment, and no selected-building, personal-property, tax-bill, payment or jurisdictional-distribution series was available from the card.

project_updates.title: Construction, suppliers and procurement audit — roles found; amounts and labor remain gaps
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Lowell Planning Board applications, memoranda, plans and minutes; City building, electrical, fuel-storage and permit searches; Exact-site web queries for permit IDs ELC202406426, ELC202409585 and ELC202507553; contractor and engineer portfolios; COMMBUYS and Massachusetts statewide IT contract records; tenant procurement disclosures; and archived trade coverage for 2015-2026. City records document renovation, a 65,000-square-foot expansion approval and later mechanical/electrical modifications. Coordinated Systems Consulting identifies its rehabilitation role and Saiful Bouquet as structural engineer, and Stantec appears in planning files, but no official downloadable reconciled permit-cost ledger, final contract amount, invoice, audited annual construction outlay, equipment-versus-building split, construction headcount, worker hours, payroll, residence, vendor payment or local-purchase share was found. Third-party permit valuations were not substituted for direct expenditure evidence or summed.

project_updates.title: Operations and workforce audit — dated headcounts and local-resident subset added
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Lowell TIF tables and annual certified-project reports; Massachusetts EDIP annual-report and compliance material; Markley careers, staff and facility pages; job boards; customer and tenant records; workforce-development, apprenticeship and local-hiring searches; and state procurement records for 2015-2026. The account adds 26 employees in 2019, 31 in December 2020, and 101 full-time permanent employees at the Lowell location on December 31, 2025, including a non-additive subset of 30 Lowell residents. The report also lists 29 hires during 2025, but the available metric is a stock and the hire flow is left in source metadata. No annual-average FTE, occupation table, wage, payroll, hours, contractor/customer headcount, turnover, county-resident total, procurement payment or selected-building employment was found.

project_updates.title: Resource, utility and environmental audit — permit equipment added; consumption remains unallocated
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: MassDEP air-plan applications, notices and OADR decisions under 24-AQ02F-0001-APP/NE-25-002; Lowell Planning Board, Sustainability Council, water, sewer and data-center materials; fuel-storage licensing; National Grid and Massachusetts DPU dockets and tariffs; ISO New England queue and reliability material; EPA facility searches; Markley facility, PPA and sustainability pages; and 2025-2026 news reports based on water bills or operator statements. The permit-listed facility total of 27 emergency generators is retained, distinct from installation and operation. AP reports an operator-stated summer peak of about 118,000 gallons per day, but no meter ledger or annual total was published and the evidence vocabulary has no direct actual peak-water metric. A Markley solar PPA covers a broader company purchase in Eversource territory and is not allocated to the National Grid-served Lowell site. No facility annual electricity, demand, tariff payment, grid-upgrade cost, verified annual water/wastewater, generator runtime, fuel use, actual emissions or selected-building resource series was found.

project_updates.title: Community-recipient audit — one recipient-verified Lowell contribution added
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: University of Massachusetts Lowell, Middlesex Community College, Greater Lowell Community Foundation, Lowell Public Schools, youth sports, libraries, housing and food-assistance recipients; City packets; Markley press and social pages; and local news archives for grants, sponsorships, donations, STEM, education and volunteer support from 2015-2026. UMass Lowell lists Markley Group in the $25,000 Signature Sponsor tier for the Meehan Student Center dedication, providing a recipient-side amount. Operator-side references to other local sponsorships and aggregate giving lacked matching recipient ledgers or defensible facility allocation and are not combined. No complete annual Middlesex County grant register, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour series or campus-attributable community total was found.

project_updates.title: Structured-data and modeling audit — no defensible residual or county-effect model
project_updates.notes: Repository county economic panels for 2001-2024, study-county exclusions, inventory history and the direct evidence documented above were reviewed. The November 2015 operating anchor leaves a pre-period, but Markley is not Middlesex County's first known data-center operation: the repository's governed first-entry research documents earlier colocation activity in Somerville, and Markley itself had later 2018-2026 expansions that prevent a single stable treatment boundary. No project-specific construction payroll, supplier spending, operating payroll, annual resource quantity compatible with the evidence metrics, same-scope public cost or causal county outcome anchors were found. No construction, supplier, household, resource, fiscal-net, input-output, difference-in-differences, event-study, synthetic-control or descriptive county-comparison model is added; arbitrary transferred assumptions would create false precision rather than a bounded estimate. No records requests were made.
